    m, n = len(a), len(b)
    # dp[i][j] = distance between a[:i] and b[:j]
    dp = [[0] * (n + 1) for _ in range(m + 1)]

    # base cases
    for i in range(m + 1):
        dp[i][0] = i
    for j in range(n + 1):
        dp[0][j] = j

    # last occurrence positions for characters in a
    last_a = {}

    for i in range(1, m + 1):
        last_b = 0  # last column where b[j-1] matched a[i-1]
        for j in range(1, n + 1):
            cost = 0 if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1] else 1
            dp[i][j] = min(
                dp[i - 1][j] + 1,          # deletion
                dp[i][j - 1] + 1,          # insertion
                dp[i - 1][j - 1] + cost    # substitution / match
            )

            # transposition of adjacent characters
            if (i > 1 and j > 1 and
                a[i - 1] == b[j - 2] and
                a[i - 2] == b[j - 1]):
                trans_cost = dp[last_a.get(b[j - 1], 0)][j - 2] + 1 + 1
                dp[i][j] = min(dp[i][j], trans_cost)

        # update last occurrence of current character in a
        last_a[a[i - 1]] = i

def schedule(jobs):
    if not jobs:
        return 0
    # sort by end time
    jobs.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])
    n = len(jobs)
    ends = [job[1] for job in jobs]
    dp = [0] * n

        j = bisect.bisect_right(ends, s) - 1

        dp[i] = max(include, exclude)

from typing import Iterable, List, Tuple, Any

def topk(stream: Iterable[Tuple[Any, Any]], k: int) -> List[Tuple[Any, Any]]:
    """
    Return the k largest (value, label) pairs from `stream`, ordered by value
    descending.  Ties are broken by arrival order (earlier items rank higher).
    The algorithm keeps at most k+1 items in memory at any time.
    """
    if k <= 0:
        return []

    # min‑heap of at most k items; each entry is (value, index, (value, label))
    heap: List[Tuple[Any, int, Tuple[Any, Any]]] = []
    idx = 0  # arrival order counter

    for item in stream:
        # item is a (value, label) tuple
        val, label = item
        entry = (val, idx, item)

        if len(heap) < k:
            heapq.heappush(heap, entry)
        else:
            # heap[0] is the smallest among the current k items
            if val > heap[0][0]:
                heapq.heapreplace(heap, entry)
            # if val == heap[0][0] we keep the earlier item (do nothing)

        idx += 1

    # Extract items in descending order of value
    result = [heapq.heappop(heap)[2] for _ in range(len(heap))]
    result.reverse()
    return result

    COUNT(c.id) AS reports
FROM staff m
JOIN chain c ON c.manager_id = m.id
GROUP BY m.id, m.name
HAVING COUNT(c.id) > 0
ORDER BY reports DESC, manager_name;
